Two ways to read a market
For a year and a half I have tried to answer one question: will this market trade like the commodities that came before it, with buyers and sellers who hedge real exposure, or will it stay a place for people who simply want a view on the price?
So far the answer has been no. We were one of the few desks willing to quote these contracts, and in March we did a
pilot trade with a broker
. After that, very little. The businesses with the most to hedge stayed away, and the people who did call wanted leverage rather than protection.

Market one: a strategic good

The first market is built on long contracts between large companies. Its counterparties sign for years at a time, and the price they agree is rarely seen by anyone else. That makes it stable, but it also makes it closed, because a newcomer has no price to hedge against and no one to hedge with.

Market two: an open one

The second market is younger and noisier. Prices move every day, contracts are short, and anyone can take part. As
the public indices
show, it is where a real price is starting to form, and where the first hedgers will come from once they trust it.
